indexableObject.name: Where intestate leaves lineal descendants not all in same degree of kindred to him, and those through whom the more remote are descended are dead.

dc.identifier.next_section.value: 41.Rules of distribution where intestate has left no lineal descendants.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
(1) If the intestate has left lineal descendants who do not all stand in the same degree of kindred to him, and the persons through whom the more remote are descended from him are dead, the property shall be divided into such a number of equal shares as may correspond with the number of the lineal descendants of the intestate who either stood in the nearest degree of kindred to him at his decease, or, having been of the like degree of kindred to him, died before him, leaving lineal descendants who survived him.
(2) One of such shares shall be allotted to each of the lineal descendants who stood in the nearest degree of kindred to the intestate at his decease; and one of such shares shall be allotted in respect of each of such deceased lineal descendants; and the share allotted in respect of each of such deceased lineal descendants shall belong to his surviving child or children or more remote lineal descendants, as the case may be; such surviving child or children or more remote lineal descendants always taking the share which his or their parent or parents would have been entitled to respectively if such parent or parents had survived the intestate.
Illustrations
(i) A had three children, John, Mary and Henry; John died, leaving four children, and Mary died, leaving one, and Henry alone survived the father. On the death of A, intestate, one-third is allotted to Henry, one-third to John's four children, and the remaining third to Mary's one child.
(ii) A left no child, but left eight grandchildren, and two children of a deceased grandchild. The property is divided into nine parts, one of which is allotted to each grandchild, and the remaining one-ninth is equally divided between the two great-grandchildren.
(iii) A has three children, John, Mary and Henry; John dies leaving four children; and one of John's children dies leaving two children. Mary dies leaving one child. A afterwards dies intestate. One-third of his property is allotted to Henry, one-third to Mary's child, and one-third is divided into four parts, one of which is allotted to each of John's three surviving children, and the remaining part is equally divided between John's two grandchildren.
(iv) A has two children, and no more, John and Mary. John dies before his father, leaving his wife pregnant. Then A dies leaving Mary surviving him, and in due time a child of John is born. A's property is to be equally divided between Mary and the posthumous child.

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Manipur University Act, 2005 
Key Provisions
1. Establishment & Governance
•	Entity: Manipur University, a Body Corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
•	Jurisdiction: Extends across Manipur, with specified oversight of outlying campuses.
•	Leadership: Chancellor: Appointed by the Central Government for a 5-year term or until 70 years of age, serving as the University's Head.
•	Central Government Oversight: Empowered to review, inspect, and direct the University, including annulment of non-compliant proceedings.
2. Academic Powers
•	Academic Authority: Offers diverse instructional programs (including semester, continuous evaluation, and choice-based credit systems).
•	Awards degrees, certificates, and honorary degrees.
•	Promotes inter-university mobility with portable pension schemes.
•	Introduces innovative courses with periodic reviews.
3. Operational & Administrative Powers
•	Resource Mobilization: Accepts benefactions, manages properties, and invests funds in approved securities.
•	Borrows money (with Central Government approval) for university development.
•	Regulatory Controls: Sets admission standards (all-India basis for national character).
•	Defines service conditions, code of conduct, and disciplinary measures for employees and students.
•	Provides advisory services to governmental and national institutions.
4. Financial & Developmental Autonomy
•	Project Undertakings: Engages in consultancy services and customised courses for co-operatives.
•	Infrastructure Development: Purchases, leases, constructs, and maintains properties for university purposes.
•	Global Engagement: Admits foreign students and explores joint degree programmes with other universities.
5. Compliance & Accountability
•	Accreditation: Seeks accreditation from renowned accrediting agencies.
•	E-Governance: Implements effective management information systems across all spheres.

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of The International Monetary Fund and Bank Act, 1945 
The International Monetary Fund and Bank Act, 1945 was enacted to implement the agreements established at the Bretton Woods Conference, facilitating India's participation in the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), which were established to promote international monetary cooperation and provide financial assistance for development projects.
Key Provisions
1.	Membership and Contributions: The act outlines the obligations of the Indian government to make financial contributions to the IMF and the IBRD. This includes payments for subscriptions and any additional sums required for India's quota in these institutions 
2.	Implementation of Agreements: It provides the legal framework for implementing the agreements under which the IMF and IBRD were established, ensuring that India adheres to the rules and regulations set forth by these international bodies 
3.	Financial Management: The act designates the Reserve Bank of India as the depository for the Indian currency holdings of the IMF and IBRD, and it outlines the procedures for managing these funds

In the Multi-Unit Co-operative Societies Act, 1942 (6 of 1942), after section 5, the following sections shall be inserted, namely:―
"5A. Transitional provisions regarding certain co-operative societies affected by reorganisation of States.―(1) Where by virtue of the provisions of Part II of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, any co-operative society which, immediately before the Ist day of November, 1956, had its objects confined to one State becomes, as from that day, a multi-unit cooperative society, it shall be deemed to be a co-operative society to which this Act applies and shall be deemed to be actually registered in the State in which the principal place of business of the cooperative society is situated.
(2) If it appears to the Central Registrar of Co-operative Societies necessary or expedient that any such society should be reconstituted or reorganised in any manner or that it should be dissolved, the Central Registrar may, with the approval of the Central Government, place before a meeting of the general body of the society held in such manner as may be prescribed by rules made under this Act, a scheme for the reconstitution, reorganisation or dissolution of the society, including proposals regarding the formation of new co-operative societies and the transfer thereto of the assets and liabilities of that society.

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of The Intelligence Organisations (Restriction of Rights) Act, 1985
Overview 
The Intelligence Organisations (Restriction of Rights) Act, 1985, is designed to regulate the conduct of members of specified Intelligence Organisations (IOs) to ensure discipline and the effective discharge of their duties. The Act imposes certain restrictions and outlines penalties for non-compliance.
Key Provisions
1.	Restrictions on IO Members: - Associations: Prohibited from being part of or associating with trade unions, labour unions, political associations, or unrecognised societies, with exceptions for purely social, recreational, or religious organizations.
•	Media Interaction: Requires prior permission from the IO head for communication with the press.
•	External Contacts: Limited regarding IO affairs, except for official duties.
•	Use of IO's Name: Prohibited without authorization.
2.	Prohibited Activities: - Participation in politically motivated meetings or demonstrations.
3.	Penalties for Non-Compliance:
•	Maximum Imprisonment: 2 years
•	Maximum Fine: ₹2,000
•	Combined Penalty: Both imprisonment and fine
4.	Nature of Offences: - Cognizability: Under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
5.	Administrative Powers: - Schedule Amendments: The Central Government can modify the list of IOs via notification.
•	Rule Making Authority: Granted to the Central Government for implementing the Act.
